title: Oncall action kit: API stream/timeouts and throttle recovery
body:
Purpose:
A compact, pragmatic oncall action kit for common API degradations we see: timeouts, 429s (rate limiting/backpressure), degraded streaming (partial chunks / stalls), and sudden elevation in 5xx/response errors. This is intentionally shorter than the full playbook — use it for first 30 minutes of triage and mitigation.

Scope & assumptions:
- Applies to Redwood public API gateway + edge proxies + serving-runtime ingress.
- Assumes access: PagerDuty, Slack #sre-oncall, Grafana dashboards, Datadog logs/traces, k8s cluster admin (kubectl), and internal routing control panel.
- Goal: restore client-visible success rate and streaming continuity, route around bad model variants, or apply graceful degradation.

High-level triage matrix (first 3 checks, do these in parallel):
1) Signal check (15s): confirm client symptoms across sources
   - Dashboards: API-error-rate, API-p50/p95 latency, streaming-chunk-latency, 429-rate.
   - Slack / Customer reports: look for correlated tickets.
   - Datadog/Logs: search for burst pattern or single-customer flood (use trace ids).
2) Scope check (60s): global? region? customer? route? model?
   - If only one region: suspect infra (AZ outage, NAT/egress).
   - If one tenant or API key: rate / client bug or abuse.
   - If specific model ID or variant: model-serving degradation or cache miss storms.
3) Hot mitigation decision (120s): pick one of these depending on scope
   - Global: engage emergency scaling + fallback routing.
   - Tenant-scoped: throttle or block offending key + notify CSM.
   - Model-scoped: route to stable model variant or reduce max_seq_len.

Immediate playbook (actions to run now):
- Communication: post to #sre-oncall, status page draft, tag "incident:api-degradation". Quick template: "Observing elevated API errors/latency in REGION X since TIME. Investigating. Will update every 10m."
- Short-term mitigations (choose applicable):
  * Increase autoscaler target for gateway / edge-proxy pool: kubectl -n infra scale deployment edge-proxy --replicas=N
  * Apply temporary global circuit-breaker to heavy routes: infra-console -> traffic-split -> reduce weight for route /v1/stream to 0.2
  * Route model requests to CPU-fallback or lower-capacity variant: routing-console -> set fallback-model: model-6B-quant -> 30%
  * Apply per-key enforcement: internal-tooling throttle key <api-key> to 10rps if one tenant causing floods.
  * Enable degraded streaming fallback: set header X-Stream-Fallback: chunked-lts to clients via ingress feature flag.
  * Cache warmup: hit model warmup endpoints for recently failed model variants to refill KV cache and lower cold-start impact.

Quick diagnosis commands and queries (use these first):
- Datadog: api.errors{env:prod,route:/v1/stream}.rollup(sum, 60) to see 429/5xx spike per minute.
- Traces: search for top-10 trace root causes during window, filter by error.code >= 500.
- Logs: grep "RequestID" and group by upstream_host to identify overloaded host.
- k8s: kubectl -n serving get pods -l app=model-serving -o wide; kubectl logs -f pod/<pod> -c runtime --tail=200
- Proxy stats: curl -s http://edge-proxy-admin/metrics | grep -E "requests_total|active_streams|429"

Common root patterns we see and tailored mitigations:
1) Cold-KV-cache storm (esp. after deploy/rolling restart)
   - Symptom: short spike in p95 latency and elevated 5xx; model nodes CPU high and disk IO for mmap.
   - Quick-mitigation: enable cold-cache soft-fallback: route small fraction to cached replicas; kick off parallel warmup requests for top N prefixes.
   - Longer fix: tune startup prewarming and reduce per-node eviction aggressiveness.

2) Client abuse / flood from single API key
   - Symptom: one consumer responsible for most of 429s and connection exhaustion.
   - Quick-mitigation: enforce per-key hard-rate-limit and return clear 429 with Retry-After; notify CSM.
   - Longer fix: blocklist temporary, quota changes, post-incident customer outreach.

3) Model variant regressions (new rollout causing increased error rates)
   - Symptom: error spike aligned with deployment time; stack traces referencing decoding / OOM.
   - Quick-mitigation: immediate rollback of model rollout or shift traffic to previous model tag.
   - Longer fix: add stricter canary metrics and synthetic prompt coverage.

4) Network egress or upstream degradation (cloud provider, NAT gateway)
   - Symptom: cross-region latency, connection resets, partial streaming stalls.
   - Quick-mitigation: switch outbound through alternate NAT zone or reroute traffic to another region.
   - Longer fix: add multi-AZ NAT, diversify egress nodes, and add retries with exponential backoff.

Streaming-specific guidance (partial chunks or stalls):
- If clients receive partial final chunk (EOF early): check model runtime logs for OOM/exit; verify chunk buffer on proxy.
- If streaming stalls mid-response: look for request-level CPU saturation on runtime node; promote warmup or reduce batch_max_tokens for streaming routes.
- Temporary mitigation: flip streaming -> poll/paginated fallback for affected routes (set header X-Prefer-Poll: yes).

429 and backpressure patterns:
- Differentiate between server-side 429 (downstream backpressure) vs client-side enforced 429 (gateway limits).
- If server-side: check queue lengths and queue_processor_lag metric; scale consumers or increase queue workers.
- If gateway-side: review rate-limiter config: limiters.yaml and per-tenant policies. Consider increasing burst window by 2x for high-SLA customers.

Operational run notes (to capture while incident is live):
- Timeline (timestamped): when alerts started, initial actions, who ran commands, decisions made (rollbacks, throttles).
- Metrics snapshots: p95/p99 latency, 429 rate, active streams, CPU per runtime node, queue backlog.
- Commands executed (copy exact command) and config changes with before/after values.

Post-incident checklist (short):
- Run automated canary against affected routes for 24h.
- Triage logs to derive root cause and add to RCA doc.
- If model regression: block the model variant from auto-rollout pipelines.
- Create action items: ticket for warmup tuning, per-key quota change, or egress architecture change.
- Update this oncall kit with one-sentence lessons learned.

Appendix: quick templates
- Slack initial post: "(incident) Observed elevated API errors on /v1/stream in us-east-1 since 10:12 UTC. Symptoms: 20% 5xx, streaming stalls. Triage in progress — scaling and routing changes underway. PD notified."
- Status page blurb: "We are investigating degraded API performance impacting streaming endpoints. Some users may experience stalls or timeouts."

Notes-to-self / TODOs for this draft:
- Add exact Grafana panel links and example Datadog queries (contribute IDs).
- Add curated warmup script snippets that ops can paste-run.
- Add approved rollback author list and runbook step to call legal for customer-facing communications if SLA breach likely.

If you're oncall and unsure: ping @Marcel Duarte in Slack and escalate via PagerDuty if client-impacting after 15 minutes.

End of kit. Keep this short, copy into incident chat, and expand into full incident writeup in confluence once stabilized.
